criteria.target: Software engineering roles at early-stage startups.
hard_requirements: Company is outside the space industry.
preferences: Small teams where software is central to the product.
AI applications, product engineering, or systems engineering; any one can establish interest.
Explicit entry-level openings are a plus, not a requirement.
Strong company fit can justify cold outreach without an advertised opening.
criteria.recommendation_policy: Return up to three recommendations with supported fit and a credible next step. Return fewer when warranted; small size alone does not establish fit.

research_limitations: This file records research already performed in this conversation; sources were not comprehensively rechecked when the file was saved.
These assessments are starting points for manual evaluation, not benchmark ground-truth labels.
Funding stages and locations under input_metadata are copied from the fixture and are not independently verified by their presence there.
Company size, funding stage, and current SWE hiring are not verified for every company.
No explicit entry-level SWE opening was verified among these ten companies. Missing evidence does not establish that no opening exists.
US location does not establish work-authorization or visa-sponsorship compatibility; those remain unknown.
Cold-outreach suggestions require identifying an appropriate recipient. No outreach was sent.

companies.fit_summary: Promising focused AI product and customer-configuration work; early-stage status and hiring remain unverified.

reasons_connected_to_profile.reason: AI calls, messaging, and booking fit Duy's interest in applying AI to a specific user workflow. MindFlow demonstrates building a working AI application with retrieval and an interactive interface; it does not establish voice-agent expertise.

Shared brand rules with location-specific settings suggest a useful conversation about product configuration. Duy's DESFire redesign demonstrates representing customer differences through reusable configuration. This is an inferred relevance connection, not evidence of an internal Adminify engineering problem.

supporting_facts.claim: Adminify markets AI agents for franchise and multi-location businesses that answer calls, engage leads, and book appointments.
The product describes centrally controlled brand standards alongside location-specific hours, services, routing, and systems.
The company-published LinkedIn page lists Lehi, Utah as headquarters.

unknowns: Current engineering team size and independently verified funding stage.
Current SWE openings and willingness to hire an early-career engineer.

Work-authorization and sponsorship compatibility.

Backend integration work is a plausible area to explore given Duy's service integration and asynchronous ingestion experience. The public product description does not establish DashFuel's architecture, throughput, or current infrastructure problems.

supporting_facts.claim: DashFuel provides petroleum distribution software including quoting, tank monitoring, dispatching, a driver app, data reconciliation, billing, and back-office integration.
The company says its software was designed and built alongside owners, dispatchers, drivers, and accountants.
The company-published LinkedIn page identifies DashFuel as a software development company headquartered in Weston, Connecticut.

DashFuel's Wellfound profile describes an early-stage remote team across the US and Europe; its jobs page showed no added jobs when checked. This profile does not independently verify current funding stage or the absence of hiring elsewhere.
